news.headline: DOJ Civil Rights Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon Resigns
news.summary: Harmeet Dhillon announced her resignation as the Department of Justice's assistant attorney general for civil rights. Sources say she planned to leave after the recent midterm elections. The departure makes her the first senior DOJ official to resign following the Democrats' sweeping midterm victories. The resignation highlights the political turnover within the Justice Department's civil rights division.

news.headline: California Governor Newsom Commutes All Death Sentences to Life Without Parole
news.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom announced that all 548 death row inmates in California will have their sentences commuted to life without parole. The action does not repeal the state's death penalty statute, so future prosecutors could seek capital punishment in new cases. Newsom framed the move as aligning with California's values and public safety goals. The decision comes as he prepares to leave office and is speculated to be a presidential candidate.

news.headline: Los Angeles mayoral race tightens between incumbent Karen Bass and challenger Nithya Raman
news.summary: Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass and progressive challenger Nithya Raman are locked in a close contest for Los Angeles mayor, with polls showing a near tie. Both candidates are defending their records on homelessness and public safety, while Bass has announced a ban on new oil and gas drilling. The race has drawn attention from various political factions, including Democratic Socialists backing Raman and establishment supporters of Bass. The outcome will shape city policy ahead of the 2028 Olympics.

news.headline: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces scrutiny after GOP midterm losses
news.summary: Republicans lost control of both chambers in Tuesday's midterm elections, prompting President Trump to ask advisers whether Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth should remain in his post. Democrats have linked the Iran war to the electoral defeat, while some GOP members warn Hegseth of a coming "reckoning" in the lame‑duck Congress. The debate centers on whether the defense secretary will be held accountable for military policy amid the new Democratic majority.

news.headline: Russell Brand convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in London
news.summary: A London jury found comedian and actor Russell Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving multiple women. The verdict was delivered at Southwark Crown Court after a trial lasting several weeks. Brand was acquitted of additional rape charges and an attempted indecent assault count. Sentencing is scheduled for the following Monday.

news.headline: Alaska Senate race probes reveal alleged ballot‑confusion scheme involving Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola
news.summary: Federal investigators sent letters to about 20 Democrats about a possible effort to recruit a candidate named Dan J. Sullivan to confuse voters in the Alaska Senate race. The race pits incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan against Democrat Mary Peltola and is extremely close under Alaska's ranked‑choice system. The DOJ inquiry and related legal challenges have drawn attention to campaign tactics and election integrity. The outcome could affect control of a Senate seat in a tightly divided chamber.

news.headline: VP JD Vance attributes GOP midterm losses to Iran war
news.summary: Vice President JD Vance said the Republican Party's defeat in the recent midterm elections was caused by voter frustration over the war in Iran and related U.S.-Israel tensions. He posted the comment on X, noting the conflict hurt the party's appeal and distancing himself from some Trump policies. The statement comes as Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate. The remark is seen as a rare public critique of the administration's foreign policy within the GOP.

news.headline: Mississippi Senate race too close to call as count nears completion
news.summary: Incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde‑Smith and Democratic challenger Scott Colom are separated by a few dozen votes with about 96% of ballots counted. An independent candidate, Ty Pinkins, also appears on the ballot. The tight margin means the final result could take days and may involve legal challenges. The outcome could affect party control of the Senate.

news.headline: First Lady Melania Trump hosts Russia and Ukraine delegations at White House
news.summary: Melania Trump arranged a meeting at the White House with representatives from Russia and Ukraine to discuss a localized ceasefire she helped broker in the frontline city of Oleshky. The ceasefire allowed humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations for six days. The event highlights the first lady's involvement in diplomatic outreach amid the ongoing war. It is being watched as a symbolic gesture of U.S. engagement in the conflict.

news.headline: Supreme Court hears case on Colorado preschool funding and LGBTQ enrollment
news.summary: The Supreme Court heard arguments in St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, a challenge by Catholic preschools to Colorado's universal preschool program. The state requires participating schools that receive public funds to admit children of same‑sex couples and transgender parents. The case pits claims of religious freedom against anti‑discrimination protections. The outcome could affect how religious institutions participate in publicly funded education programs.

satire.headline: Friends Graciously Bless Family With Meal Train Food That Will Fill Up Their Fridge Before Being Thrown In The Trash Next Week
satire.summary: BOISE, ID — The power of love and true kindness was on display this week, as a group of friends graciously blessed a local family with Meal train food that would fill up their fridge before being thrown in the trash next week.

satire.headline: After Seeing Election Results, Trump Announces Retaliatory Tariffs On America
satire.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — On Thursday morning, President Donald Trump announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States after his political party suffered massive losses in the midterm elections.
